plan: 2 Samuel 24:1-9; 1 Chronicles 21:1-6; 2 Samuel 24:10-17; 1 Chronicles 21:7-17; 2 Samuel 24:18-25; 1 Chronicles 21:18–22:1; 1 Chronicles 22:2-19

readings.title: Daviḏ Orders a Census
readings.subtitle: Yo’aḇ Numbers the People
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 24:1] And again the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’ěl, and moved Daviḏ against them to say, “Go, number <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl and <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah.”
[2] And the sovereign said to Yo’aḇ the commander of the army who was with <dn>את</dn> him, “Go please, throughout all the tribes of Yisra’ěl, from Dan to Be’ěrsheḇa, and register <dn>את</dn> the people, so that I know <dn>את</dn> the number of the people.”
[3] And Yo’aḇ said to the sovereign, “Even if <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does add to the people a hundredfold more than there are, and the eyes of my master the sovereign see it, but why does my master the sovereign delight in this matter?”
[4] However, the sovereign’s word was strong towards Yo’aḇ and against the commanders of the army. And Yo’aḇ and the commanders of the army went out from the presence of the sovereign to register <dn>את</dn> the people of Yisra’ěl.
[5] And they passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarděn and camped in Aro‛ěr, on the right side of the town which is in the midst of the wadi of Gaḏ, and toward Ya‛zěr.
[6] Then they came to Gil‛aḏ and to the land of Taḥtim Ḥoḏshi, and they came to Dan Ya‛an and around to Tsiḏon.
[7] And they came to the stronghold of Tsor and to all the cities of the Ḥivvites and the Kena‛anites, and went out to South Yehuḏah as far as Be’ěrsheḇa.
[8] And when they had gone through all the land, they came to Yerushalayim at the end of nine new moons and twenty days.
[9] And Yo’aḇ gave <dn>את</dn> the number of the registration of the people to the sovereign, and there were in Yisra’ěl eight hundred thousand brave men who drew the sword, and the men of Yehuḏah were five hundred thousand men.

readings.title: An Adversary Provokes the Census
readings.subtitle: Yo’aḇ's Reluctance
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 21:1] And Satan stood up against Yisra’ěl, and moved <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ to number <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl.
[2] And Daviḏ said to Yo’aḇ and to the rulers of the people, “Go, number <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from Be’ěrsheḇa to Dan, and bring <dn>את</dn> the number of them to me so that I know it.”
[3] And Yo’aḇ answered, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does add to <dn>His</dn> people a hundred times more than they are. But, my master the sovereign, are they not all my master’s servants? Why does my master seek to do this? Why should he be a cause of guilt in Yisra’ěl?”
[4] But the sovereign’s word was strong against Yo’aḇ. And Yo’aḇ left and went throughout all Yisra’ěl and came to Yerushalayim.
[5] And Yo’aḇ gave <dn>את</dn> the sum of the number of the people to Daviḏ. And all Yisra’ěl had one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Yehuḏah had four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew the sword.
[6] But he did not number <dn>את</dn> Lěvi and <dn>את</dn> Binyamin among them, for the sovereign’s word was loathsome to Yo’aḇ.

readings.title: Daviḏ's Repentance
readings.subtitle: Three Options of Judgment
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 24:10] And the heart of Daviḏ struck <dn>את</dn> him after he had numbered <dn>את</dn> the people. And Daviḏ said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. But now, I pray, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, take away <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of <dn>Your</dn> servant, for I have done very foolishly.”
[11] And Daviḏ rose up in the morning, and the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to the prophet Gaḏ, Daviḏ’s seer, saying,
[12] “Go, and you shall speak to Daviḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> hold three options before you. Choose one of them, and <dn>I</dn> do it to you.”</dq> ’ ”
[13] Gaḏ then came to Daviḏ and informed him. And he said to him, “Should seven years of scarcity of food come to you in your land? Or would you flee three new moons before your enemies, while they pursue you? Or should there be three days’ plague in your land? Now know and see what answer I take back to <dn>Him</dn> who sent me.”
[14] And Daviḏ said to Gaḏ, “I am in great trouble. Please let us fall into the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>His</dn> compassion is great, but do not let me fall into the hand of man.”
[15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent a plague upon Yisra’ěl from the morning till the appointed time, and from Dan to Be’ěrsheḇa seventy thousand men of the people died.
[16] And the messenger stretched out <dn>His</dn> hand over Yerushalayim to destroy it, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> relented concerning the evil, and said to the messenger who was destroying the people, <dq>“It is enough, now stop <dn>Your</dn> hand.”</dq> And the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was by the threshing-floor of Aravnah the Yeḇusite.
[17] And Daviḏ spoke to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> when he saw <dn>את</dn> the messenger who was striking the people, and said, “See, I have sinned, and I have done perversely. But these sheep, what have they done? Let <dn>Your</dn> hand, I pray, be against me and against my father’s house.”

readings.title: The Judgment of Elohim
readings.subtitle: The Messenger at the Threshing-Floor
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 21:7] And it was evil in the eyes of <dn>Elohim</dn>, concerning this matter, and <dn>He</dn> struck <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl.
[8] Then Daviḏ said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “I have sinned greatly, because I have done <dn>את</dn> this matter. But now, I pray, take away <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of <dn>Your</dn> servant, for I have done very foolishly.”
[9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Gaḏ, Daviḏ’s seer, saying,
[10] “Go, and you shall speak to Daviḏ, saying, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> hold three options before you – choose one of them for yourself, and <dn>I</dn> do it to you.”</dq> ’ ”
[11] So Gaḏ came to Daviḏ and said to him, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Choose for yourself</dq>
[12] <dq>either three years of scarcity of food, or three new moons to be defeated by your foes with the sword of your enemies overtaking you, or else for three days the sword of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even the plague in the land, with the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> destroying throughout all the borders of Yisra’ěl.’</dq> And now consider what answer I am to return to <dn>Him</dn> who sent me.”
[13] And Daviḏ said to Gaḏ, “I am in great trouble. Please let me fall into the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>His</dn> compassion is very great, but do not let me fall into the hand of man.”
[14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent a plague upon Yisra’ěl, and seventy thousand men of Yisra’ěl fell.
[15] And <dn>Elohim</dn> sent a messenger to Yerushalayim to destroy it. And as he was destroying, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw, and relented about the evil, and said to the messenger who was destroying, <dq>“Enough! Now stop your hand.”</dq> And the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was standing by the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite.
[16] And Daviḏ lifted <dn>את</dn> his eyes and saw <dn>את</dn> the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> standing between earth and the heavens, having in his hand a drawn sword stretched out over Yerushalayim. And Daviḏ and the elders, wrapped in sackcloth, fell on their faces.
[17] And Daviḏ said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Was it not I who commanded the people to be numbered? I am the one who has sinned and done evil indeed. But these, the sheep, what have they done? Let <dn>Your</dn> hand, I pray, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, be against me and my father’s house, but not against <dn>Your</dn> people, to be plagued.”

readings.title: Daviḏ Builds a Slaughter-Place
readings.subtitle: The Plague is Withdrawn
readings.text:
[2 Samuel 24:18] And Gaḏ came that day to Daviḏ and said to him, “Go up, raise a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the threshing-floor of Aravnah the Yeḇusite.”
[19] And Daviḏ, according to the word of Gaḏ, went up as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded.
[20] And Aravnah looked and saw <dn>את</dn> the sovereign and <dn>את</dn> his servants coming toward him. And Aravnah went out and bowed before the sovereign with his face to the ground.
[21] And Aravnah said, “Why has my master the sovereign come to his servant?” And Daviḏ said, “To buy <dn>את</dn> the threshing-floor from you, to build a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so that the plague be withdrawn from the people.”
[22] And Aravnah said to Daviḏ, “Let my master the sovereign take and offer that which seems good to him. Here are cattle for ascending offering, and threshing implements and the yokes of the cattle for wood.
[23] “All these, O sovereign, Aravnah has given to the sovereign.” And Aravnah said to the sovereign, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> accept you!”
[24] And the sovereign said to Aravnah, “No, let me buy it from you for a price, for certain. I am not offering ascending offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn> without cost.” So Daviḏ bought <dn>את</dn> the threshing-floor and <dn>את</dn> the cattle for fifty sheqels of silver.
[25] And Daviḏ built a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> there, and offered ascending offerings and peace offerings. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered the prayers for the land, and the plague was withdrawn from Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Site for the Temple
readings.subtitle: Fire from the Heavens
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 21:18] And the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Gaḏ to say to Daviḏ that Daviḏ should go up to raise a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite.
[19] So Daviḏ went up at the word of Gaḏ, which he had spoken in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[20] And Ornan turned and saw <dn>את</dn> the messenger. And his four sons with him hid themselves, and Ornan was threshing wheat.
[21] And Daviḏ came to Ornan, and Ornan looked and saw <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ, and he went out from the threshing-floor, and bowed down to Daviḏ with his face to the ground.
[22] And Daviḏ said to Ornan, “Give me <dn>את</dn> the site of the threshing-floor, so that I build a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on it. Give it to me at the complete price, so that the plague is restrained from the people.”
[23] And Ornan said to Daviḏ, “Take it for yourself, and let my master the sovereign do what is good in his eyes. See, I shall give you the cattle for ascending offerings, the threshing implements for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I give it all.”
[24] And Sovereign Daviḏ said to Ornan, “No, but I shall certainly buy it at the complete price, for I do not take what is yours for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor offer an ascending offering without cost.”
[25] And Daviḏ gave Ornan six hundred sheqels of gold by weight for the place.
[26] And Daviḏ built there a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and offered ascending offerings and peace offerings, and called on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>He</dn> answered him from the heavens by fire on the slaughter-place of ascending offering.
[27] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded the messenger, and he returned his sword to its sheath.
[28] At that time, when Daviḏ saw that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had answered him on the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite, he slaughtered there,
[29] for the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the slaughter-place of the ascending offering, which Mosheh had made in the wilderness, were at that time at the high place in Giḇ‛on.
[30] But Daviḏ was unable to go before it to inquire of <dn>Elohim</dn>, for he was afraid of the sword of the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[1 Chronicles 22:1] Daviḏ then said, “This is the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and this is the slaughter-place of ascending offering for Yisra’ěl.”

readings.title: Daviḏ Prepares Materials
readings.subtitle: The Promise Concerning Shelomoh
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 22:2] And Daviḏ commanded to gather <dn>את</dn> the foreigners who were in the land of Yisra’ěl. And he appointed stonemasons to cut hewn stones to build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[3] And Daviḏ prepared large quantities of iron for the nails of the doors of the gates and for the clamps, and more bronze than could be weighed,
[4] and cedar trees beyond number, for the Tsiḏonians and those from Tsor brought much cedar wood to Daviḏ.
[5] And Daviḏ said, “Shelomoh my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be built for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is to be exceedingly great, for a splendid Name, to all the lands. Please, let me make preparation for it.” So Daviḏ made extensive preparations before his death.
[6] He also called for his son Shelomoh, and commanded him to build a house for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl.
[7] And Daviḏ said to Shelomoh, “My son, as for me, it has been in my heart to build a house to the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>,
[8] but the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, <dq>‘You have shed much blood and have fought great battles. You do not build a house for <dn>My</dn> Name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in <dn>My</dn> presence.</dq>
[9] <dq>See, a son is to be born to you, who is a man of rest. And <dn>I</dn> shall give him rest from all his enemies all around, for Shelomoh is his name, and peace and rest <dn>I</dn> give to Yisra’ěl in his days.</dq>
[10] <dq>He does build a house for <dn>My</dn> Name, and he is to be <dn>My</dn> son, and <dn>I</dn> am to be his <dn>Father</dn>. And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of his reign over Yisra’ěl forever.’</dq>

readings.title: Instructions to Shelomoh
readings.subtitle: A Charge to the Rulers
readings.text:
[1 Chronicles 22:11] “Now, my son, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be with you, then you shall prosper and build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has said to you.
[12] “Only, let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> give you wisdom and understanding, and command you concerning Yisra’ěl, so that you guard <dn>את</dn> the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>,
[13] then you shall prosper, if you guard to do <dn>את</dn> the laws and <dn>את</dn> right-rulings with which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh concerning Yisra’ěl. Be strong and brave, do not fear nor be discouraged.
[14] “See, in my affliction I have prepared for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond measure, for it is plenty. And I have prepared timber and stone, and you shall add to them.
[15] “And with you there are many workmen: hewers and workers of stone and timber, and all types of skilled men for every kind of work.
[16] “Of gold and silver and bronze and iron there is no limit. Rise up and do, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you.”
[17] And Daviḏ commanded all the rulers of Yisra’ěl to help Shelomoh his son, saying,
[18] “Is not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with you? And has <dn>He</dn> not given you rest all around? For <dn>He</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and before <dn>His</dn> people.
[19] “Now, give your heart and your being to seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And rise up and build <dn>את</dn> the set-apart place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, to bring <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the set-apart vessels of <dn>Elohim</dn> into the house that is to be built for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
